Affiliation:: University of Oklahoma, School of Computer Science / University of Houston - Clear Lake
Data & Platforms: Intel dual core with 3.06GHz clock speed
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Model-Driven Approach: A composite prediction model combining CPU availability and memory models to estimate execution efficiency, providing upper and lower bounds for CPU availability and memory usage, and an empirical average CPU availability model (validated through extensive case studies and experimental studies).

Analytical Framework: Theoretically derived upper and lower bound formulas for CPU availability, validated through extensive experimental studies, demonstrating low variation in CPU availability when aggregate CPU loading is low or high.

Performance Prediction Model: A model to forecast execution efficiency of GPUs for computationally intensive kernels, validated with Nvidia CUDA GPU SDK benchmark program, showing a prediction error of 0.13-5.69%.

Dynamic Scheduling Algorithm Enhancement: Using partial feedback and biasing model requirements to enhance the robustness of dynamic scheduling algorithms in distributed systems, demonstrating the necessity of complete feedback and the effectiveness of proposed biasing strategies.
Summary Description: John Antonio is a researcher specializing in computer science, with a focus on computer architecture, operating systems, and parallel computing. His work primarily involves developing models and frameworks for predicting and optimizing performance in multi-core systems, GPUs, and distributed systems. He employs a model-driven approach, combining CPU availability and memory models to estimate execution efficiency, and has developed analytical frameworks for estimating CPU availability and performance prediction models for GPUs. His research aims to improve execution efficiency, predict resource availability, and optimize performance in heterogeneous environments.
